items.stimulus: For decades, a rail line through the center of Tallmere carried freight past warehouses that had long since closed. In 2019, the city converted the abandoned corridor into a four-mile greenway, ______ residents with a car-free route linking three neighborhoods that had previously been divided by the tracks. Within two years, counts showed that more than 3,000 people used the path on an average weekday.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The sentence already has a subject and main verb: "the city converted." What follows the comma is a descriptive add-on telling what the conversion did, so it needs a participle, not another tensed verb. "Providing" is the "-ing" form because the conversion causes the result, and it attaches cleanly to the clause before it.

B.why: You added a second tensed verb, "provides," after "converted" with no conjunction joining them. Without "and," two main verbs can't sit side by side, and the present tense also clashes with the past-tense "converted."

C.why: "It provides" is a complete independent clause. Putting it after a comma with no conjunction creates a comma splice. You needed a modifier here, not a new sentence.

D.why: "Has provided" is a finite verb competing with "converted" for the same subject, and nothing like "and" connects them. The main clause was already complete, so the blank needed a participle.
